d.d: To use caution, pay attention to (used both with and without of).
Baffled, confused, mystified, at a loss, not thinking clearly, or uncertain.
d.x: He was just standing there, turning this way and that, with a bewildered look on his face.

d.d: simple past and past participle of bewilder
Very baffling, confusing, or perplexing, often due to a very large choice being available.
d.x: There was a bewildering collection of curiosities filling the room.

d.d: present participle and gerund of bewilder

d.x: I was bewitched by the sight of the girl dancing in the forest.

d.d: Under a spell; subject to an act of witchcraft.
entranced, charmed, fascinated, as though subject to a magical influence.
simple past and past participle of bewitch
The act by which somebody is bewitched; a curse or enchantment.
